old_caption: The video depicts a close-up scene where a person is holding a white paper towel with a textured surface. The individual's hand is visible, gripping the paper towel firmly. In the background, there is a rough, gray concrete surface, suggesting an outdoor setting. A small flame is already burning at one corner of the paper towel, consuming material at that corner. The hand holding the paper towel remains steady throughout the sequence, ensuring the paper towel stays in view while the fire spreads along the edge, consuming more material and increasing in size.
original_wisa_caption: The video depicts a close-up scene where a person is holding a white paper towel with a textured surface. The individual's hand is visible, gripping the paper towel firmly. In the background, there is a rough, gray concrete surface, suggesting an outdoor setting. Another hand appears from the right side of the frame, holding a green lighter. The lighter is brought close to the paper towel, and a small flame ignites on one corner of the paper towel. As the flame spreads, it creates a small, flickering area of light and smoke. The fire gradually grows larger, consuming more of the paper towel. The hand holding the paper towel remains steady throughout the sequence, ensuring the paper towel stays in view while the fire spreads. The video captures the progression of the fire from a small spark to a more substantial blaze, all within the confined space of the paper towel.
caption: The video depicts a close-up, slightly top-down view of a hand holding a white paper napkin flat over a gray concrete surface. The upper-right corner of the napkin is already alight when the clip starts, a small orange-yellow flame licking along a brown-to-black charred margin. This flame persists throughout, flickering in shape and brightness. Sometimes it forms a single tongue, sometimes splitting into two. As the burning continues, the charred region gradually enlarges and the paper edge is visibly eaten away, so the burnt hole grows. A second, partly visible clenched hand remains at the top-right edge of the frame the whole time. The holding thumb grips the lower edge of the napkin and shifts slightly, drifting the sheet within the frame. Over the course of the clip the napkin's fold reads differently, with a lifted flap or second layer becoming apparent on the left as the whole sheet tilts. The fire stays anchored at the corner and continues burning through the final frame.

without inventing how it began or how it ultimately ends. A process may already be happening
on the first frame and still be happening after the last. Do not force the endpoints to match,
infer a physical error from their mismatch, or manufacture continuity across a visible edit.
Use the chronological video as primary evidence. The independent visual notes are fallible aids,
not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.
You receive the original WISA caption's stylistic profile, without its possibly wrong facts.
Retain its English narrative voice, viewpoint, paragraph structure and level of visual detail.
Aim for 85-115% of the original WISA word count,
and retain supported scene details while clearly describing the main visible process. Do not
replace it with a short keyword prompt, physics explanation, checklist or a generic summary.
Correct wrong subjects, actions, directions, contacts, temporal ordering and completion claims.
Distinguish an already ongoing process from a new event actually visible within this excerpt.
Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
Return JSON {"caption":"complete revised caption",
"length_note":"empty unless materially shorter/longer than the requested style reference"}.
